proposed_widenings.name: Attachment.floating_points
proposed_widenings.justification: Dancing Lights places up to 4 lights at discrete hovering positions anywhere within 120 ft — not attached to a creature, not the caster (self), and not a geometric area emanating from a single origin. The existing Attachment variants (self, target, area, mark, object) all presuppose either a creature anchor or a fixed geometric shape from a single origin point. AnchorTarget.location exists for planted spell triggers but is unavailable in the ongoing-effect attachment vocabulary.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You create up to four torch-size lights within range, making them appear as torches, lanterns, or glowing orbs that hover for the duration.

proposed_widenings.name: reposition_attachment
proposed_widenings.justification: The Bonus Action lets the caster move the lights up to 60 feet to another space within range. The on_caster_spends_action trigger exists and fits perfectly, but the resulting effect — repositioning the spell's floating attachment origin(s) — has no corresponding atom. force_move and teleport both apply to creatures. No atom moves a non-creature effect attachment.
proposed_widenings.evidence: As a Bonus Action, you can move the lights up to 60 feet to a space within range.

notes: Core atoms all exist: create_illusion (Dancing Lights is listed as a pressure case in types.ts), emit_light (0 bright + 10 ft dim), on_caster_spends_action (bonus_action cost), CastTimeEffectModeChoice (4 lights vs humanlike form), caster_recasts_spell duration-end trigger. The two surface gaps block honest encoding: (1) attaching a floating-point ongoing effect to discrete spatial positions rather than creatures/self/area, and (2) expressing the reposition result of the bonus action spend.
